packageRules.description: Wait 14 days after a release before proposing it, for every update Renovate can date. Set here because a matching package rule overrides the top-level setting. Vulnerability fixes skip the wait.
Pinning a version already in use is not an upgrade, so it is not delayed.

A major update can drop support for older systems that adopters run, so it waits for the owner's approval on the dependency dashboard (DR-111). Minor and patch updates are proposed as usual, and so are vulnerability fixes, which the vulnerabilityAlerts block above lets through without approval.

The Python that the project develops on stays at the oldest release that the tool supports, which .python-version holds and the pyenv manager alone reads, so Renovate proposes no newer one; CI also tests the newest release (DR-134, DR-265).

An update of OpenSpec or Superpowers changes files that steer agent sessions, so its pull request says how they are refreshed and that no agent session starts on its branch before the owner has read its refreshed diff (DR-265).
prBodyNotes: Before this merges, the owner reads this diff. Its generated or vendored files are then refreshed on this branch from a working tree outside any agent session's folder, by `scripts/verify-openspec.sh` for OpenSpec, which writes the generated skills again, or by `scripts/sync-superpowers.sh` for Superpowers, and the owner reads the refreshed diff before merging. No agent session starts on this branch before the owner has read its refreshed diff.

customManagers.description: vendor/superpowers is a pinned copy of an upstream release. This moves sha= and tag= together across releases; CI re-syncs the tree from sha= and fails on any difference, so a bump also needs scripts/sync-superpowers.sh run on its branch. ignorePaths above restates the preset's list without **/vendor/** so that this file is read.
